adds.title: LGBT rights in Mexico - Wikipedia (state-by-state coverage including Sonora)
adds.summary: The page's state-by-state coverage names Sonora as one of the 25 Mexican states that have legislated a gender identity law, with Sonora dated to 2020, giving trans people a statutory procedure to rectify gender on civil documents. It further records that Sonora's Congress banned conversion therapies (ECOSIG) on 6 December 2022, and that Sonora is among the states whose hate-crime laws recognize motivation by gender and sexual preference and which ratified the 2011 constitutional amendment prohibiting discrimination on grounds of sexual orientation. On marriage, the page records that by 31 December 2022 every Mexican state, including Sonora, had legalized same-sex marriage by legislation, executive order or judicial ruling. For this record: concrete Sonora-specific legal protections (gender-recognition procedure, conversion-therapy ban, hate-crime framework, marriage availability) that the current summary said were unsupported by vetted sources.

adds.title: Aprueban Ley de Identidad de Género en Sonora - El Sol de Hermosillo
adds.summary: Hermosillo-based daily El Sol de Hermosillo (article dated 1 October 2020) reports that Sonora's Congress approved the state's Gender Identity Law ("Ley de Identidad de Género"), under which people who identify with the opposite gender can modify their official documentation. For this record: local-news confirmation that Sonora legislated a gender-recognition procedure for trans people in 2020, the state-level fact the country dossier currently lacks, and one of the procedures counted in the report that 22 of Mexico's 32 states have enacted such laws.

adds.title: LGBTQ rights in Australia - Wikipedia (South Australia-specific provisions)
adds.summary: The page's South Australia-specific coverage records that the state was the first Australian jurisdiction to decriminalise male homosexual activity (law commenced 2 October 1975) and that it is the only jurisdiction whose scheme for historical gay convictions is 'spent' rather than expunged (Spent Convictions (Decriminalised Offences) Amendment Act 2013 in force 22 December 2013). It records South Australian registered domestic relationships from 1 August 2017, same-sex marriage from December 2017 under the federal Act, and that South Australia was the last state to abolish the gay-panic defence (December 2020, taking effect 1 April 2021). It also records the South Australian conversion-therapy ban (passed September 2024, law effective April 2025) and that, with the ACT, South Australia was one of the first two jurisdictions to allow the sex recorded on a birth certificate to be changed without sex-reassignment surgery (2016 Act). For this record: the state's own legal framework for documents, relationships and criminal-record history, giving the region-specific signals the current summary says the dossier lacks.

adds.title: LGBTQ rights in South Australia - Wikipedia (dedicated article)
adds.summary: Dedicated state article recording that since 23 May 2017 (Births, Deaths and Marriages Registration (Gender Identity) Amendment Act 2016, royal assent 15 December 2016) a South Australian can change the sex descriptor on a birth certificate with appropriate clinical treatment, with no sex-reassignment surgery or forced divorce if married; non-binary and 'indeterminate' sex descriptors are also available on state birth certificates. It records the hate-crime sentencing laws explicitly including sexual orientation, gender identity and intersex characteristics, passed and implemented November 2021; the gay-panic defence abolished on 1 December 2020 and effective 1 April 2021; and the Conversion Practices Prohibition Act 2024, passed October 2024 and in legal effect 1 April 2025. It also records that the state's Equal Opportunity Act 1984 was amended in 2016 to protect gender identity and sexual orientation, that same-sex couples could adopt from 17 February 2017, and that same-sex marriage has been legal since December 2017 (the 2017 postal survey returning 62.5% 'Yes' in South Australia). For this record: the state-level statute and enforcement facts (especially the birth-certificate marker regime and hate-crime sentencing) that the current summary says are undocumented for South Australia.
